title: The Leaf-Darkness Where Direction Dissolves

features.name: canopy thickness
features.desc-on-touch: Leaves so dense that compass becomes poetry. Direction here is measured in surrender—you stop trying to know which way and start learning to walk into what grows.

features.name: spiral descent
features.desc-on-touch: Roots twisting in such a way that north becomes a suggestion, then a memory, then a language you never learned. The spiral teaches: getting lost is how the forest holds you.

features.name: depth marker plant
features.desc-on-touch: A growth that has given up on reaching the sky. It only grows toward the darkness, teaching that down is just another kind of up.

features.name: lost walker's rest
features.desc-on-touch: A small clearing where you can sit and let the forest teach you that being lost is not a problem to solve. It is an invitation to listen.

features.name: navigation pool
features.desc-on-touch: Black water reflecting leaves instead of sky. Here the reflection teaches: there is no wrong direction if you stop expecting directions to mean arrival.

features.name: glyph of dissolution
features.desc-on-touch: A mark carved by time and water—a map that unmaps itself. North is here, then there, then nowhere. The glyph is the archive's admission: some paths only teach by losing you.

inscription: here the forest learned that being lost is the same as being found in water

file.name: Leaf_Darkness_Navigation_Recording_Lost_Voices.wav
file.note: Two voices, disoriented, learning to walk without direction. The canopy teaches: surrender is the only compass that works here.

reverie.title: REVERIE — walking without direction
narr: the canopy is so thick that the sky is only memory now.
she walks ahead, then you cannot tell ahead from behind.
the leaves fall so thick they sound like rain.
you have been lost for hours—or were you ever anywhere?
she stops, laughing. you stop. there is no ground beneath knowing.
the forest wraps around you both like sleep. you are not afraid.

exits.label: back to the canopy where water learned to breathe
toward the deeper dark where even the leaves have forgotten their names
down into the understory where the roots keep their own records
